# gitmoap_group_pipeline_variable (Resource)

Sets the variable for the pipelines of every repository beneath the group, unless a nearer group or the repository declares the same name. Mark it secret and the value is stored write-only and never returned. Only the group's Owners may write group variables, since they reach repositories whose Maintainers never see the change. Names the platform reserves are refused, and a group holds a limited number of variables.

The token needs `pipeline_variable:manage` and `pipeline_variable:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "registry_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "platform" {
  full_path = "acme/platform"
}

resource "gitmoap_group_pipeline_variable" "region" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.platform.group_id
  name     = "DEPLOY_REGION"
  value    = "eu-west-1"
}

# A secret value is never returned by the API, and value_wo keeps it out of Terraform's state too.
resource "gitmoap_group_pipeline_variable" "registry_token" {
  group_id         = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.platform.group_id
  name             = "REGISTRY_TOKEN"
  value_wo         = var.registry_token
  value_wo_version = 1
  secret           = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The group's id
- `name` (String)

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `protected` (Boolean) Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag receives the variable: one a branch or tag
rule protects, building a commit in that ref's history. A run on any other ref receives
neither this value nor a value the same name has further up, and a step whose config reads
it is refused. Defaults to `false`.
- `secret` (Boolean) Whether the value is a secret. A secret's value can never be read back and is redacted from
step logs; either way every step receives it as an environment variable. Defaults to
`false`.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The variable's value. Absent for a secret, whose value can be written but never read back. Or set `value_wo`, to keep it out of the state.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Sets `value` without keeping it in Terraform's plan or state: write-only, with Terraform 1.11 and later. Change `value_wo_version` to send it again.
- `value_wo_version` (Number) A number to change when `value_wo` changes, to send it again: Terraform can't tell, since it doesn't keep it.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `updated_at` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and name, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_group_pipeline_variable.example "<group_id>/<name>"
```
